title: Biliary tract cancer
subtitle: Gallbladder · intrahepatic, perihilar and distal cholangiocarcinoma · one systemic backbone, four different operations, and a molecular profile that depends entirely on where the tumor sits
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Gallbladder Cancer and Cholangiocarcinoma (Northness A, Heestand G) · NCCN · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Four diseases in one name
rows: Arises proximal to the second-order ducts. The molecularly rich one — FGFR2 and IDH1 live here
At the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts. Resection planned by Bismuth-Corlette class
Common bile duct up to, but not including, the ampulla
<5,000 cases/yr US; fundus 60% > body 30% > neck 10%. 1–2% are found incidentally at cholecystectomy for stones
blocks.footnote: ~8,000 cholangiocarcinomas/yr in the US, median age ~70. The subtypes share systemic therapy but differ in staging system, operation, and molecular profile — which is why anatomic site has to be stated before anything else. Risk: CCA — PSC, HBV/HCV, liver flukes, male sex, obesity, diabetes, alcohol. GBC — cholelithiasis, gallbladder calcification, female sex, chronic Salmonella or H. pylori infection.

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Labs: CBC with differential, CMP, PT/INR, CA 19-9, HBV and HCV serologies
Imaging: triphasic CT abdomen/pelvis or liver-protocol MRI + CT chest to complete staging. PET/CT to exclude occult disease when the plan is resection
Gallbladder: start with ultrasound — go to triphasic CT or MRI for a polyp >10 mm or wall thickening not explained by cholecystitis
MRCP to plan biopsy and stenting. ERCP to stent, decompress and brush — brushings are often non-diagnostic, so go to EUS-FNA when they are
Genomically profile every tumor, and send MMR, HER2 IHC and PD-L1. This is not optional in biliary cancer — roughly a third of patients have a level 1/2 actionable alteration
If perihilar CCA might go to transplant, do NOT perform a transperitoneal biopsy — tumor seeding disqualifies the patient from the protocol

boxes: treat as metastatic — gem/cis + durvalumab or pembrolizumab
ablative RT gives excellent local control; ABC-07 was negative
HAI floxuridine and Y-90 rest on single-arm phase 2 data
Start chemo-IO and profile in parallel
send NGS, MMR and HER2 IHC on day one
targeted therapy if an alteration was found — see page 2

blocks.heading: Staging — three separate AJCC systems
rows: Size and vascular invasion: T1a ≤5 cm / T1b >5 cm, both without vascular invasion · T2 vascular invasion or multiple tumors · T3 perforates visceral peritoneum · T4 direct extrahepatic invasion. N is simply N0 / N1

Depth then vessels: T1 confined to the duct · T2a into surrounding fat, T2b into hepatic parenchyma · T3 unilateral portal vein or hepatic artery branch · T4 main portal vein bilaterally, common hepatic artery, or second-order radicals with contralateral vessel
Millimetres of duct-wall invasion: T1 <5 mm · T2 5–12 mm · T3 >12 mm · T4 celiac axis, SMA or common hepatic artery

Which side of the wall: T1a lamina propria, T1b muscularis · T2a peritoneal side, T2b hepatic side — the distinction drives the operation · T3 serosa, liver or one adjacent organ · T4 main portal vein / hepatic artery or ≥2 organs
blocks.footnote: Nodes: perihilar, distal and gallbladder all use N1 = 1–3 nodes, N2 = ≥4. Intrahepatic uses N0/N1 only.

blocks.heading: Surgery — the only curative option
items: Most patients are unresectable at presentation, and most resected patients still recur
Resectability requires: no retropancreatic or paraceliac nodes, no distant liver metastases, no main portal vein or hepatic artery invasion, no adjacent-organ invasion, no dissemination
Intrahepatic → hepatic lobectomy; 5-yr OS 11–40%. Perihilar → en bloc resection by Bismuth-Corlette class. Distal → Whipple + extrahepatic duct; 5-yr OS 10–40%
Gallbladder: T1a is cured by simple cholecystectomy alone. T1b and above need en bloc cholecystectomy + resection of liver segments 4a/4b + regional lymphadenectomy
Incidentally discovered gallbladder cancer beyond T1a must go back to the operating room for the 4a/4b bed resection and lymphadenectomy
Liver transplant is an option for highly selected perihilar CCA (Mayo protocol: mass ≤3 cm, no transperitoneal biopsy, no metastases) — intention-to-treat 5-yr survival ~53%

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — molecular profiling, which is where biliary cancer is won or lost

blocks.heading: Alteration by site — why site matters
blocks.footnote: FGFR2 and IDH1 are intrahepatic diseases and are mutually exclusive. HER2 is a gallbladder and extrahepatic disease. Roughly a third of all biliary cancers carry a level 1/2 actionable alteration — but that is ~40% of intrahepatic versus ~15% of extrahepatic. Western cohorts (AACR GENIE); in East Asian series IDH1 and FGFR2 fall and KRAS rises.

blocks.heading: Living with an FGFR inhibitor
items: Hyperphosphatemia is on-target, not idiosyncratic — FGFR1 blockade removes the FGF23 phosphaturic signal. It is a marker that the drug is working. Pemigatinib ~60%, futibatinib ~85%, lirafugratinib ~21%. Manage with a low-phosphate diet, sevelamer, and dose holds
Ocular toxicity: serous retinopathy / retinal pigment epithelial detachment, plus dry eye in over 20%. Baseline and serial ophthalmology with OCT — roughly q2 months for 6 months, then q3 months
Nail and hair: onycholysis in ~47%, alopecia in a third. Stomatitis, arthralgia and diarrhea are common

Resistance arrives at ~6–9 months as polyclonal secondary FGFR2 kinase-domain mutations, classically the gatekeeper V564F. The covalent agents (futibatinib, lirafugratinib) retain activity against some but not all of these

blocks.heading: Driver → therapy
rows: FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement ~12% of iCCA

All second-line and beyond. Lirafugratinib (FGFR2-selective; approved 23 Sep 2026) — ORR 46%, DOR 11.8 mo, and notably less hyperphosphatemia (~21%). Futibatinib ORR 42% (accelerated; label is intrahepatic only). Pemigatinib ORR 37% (accelerated, any site). Only fusions and rearrangements qualify — point mutations do not. FIGHT-302 moved pemigatinib to 1L on PFS but showed no OS gain, and the 1L indication is not approved. Infigratinib was withdrawn in 2024

Ivosidenib after 1–2 prior lines (regular approval). PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 months, HR 0.37 — statistically emphatic, clinically modest. Unadjusted OS was not significant (10.3 vs 7.5 mo) because 70% crossed over; crossover-adjusted HR 0.49

Zanidatamab — the only BTC-specific approval (accelerated, Nov 2024), IHC 3+ only, 2L+: ORR 52% in IHC 3+, DOR 14.9 mo. T-DXd is covered by the tumor-agnostic IHC 3+ approval, but ILD reached 17% in the biliary cohort — higher than in most tumor types. Trastuzumab + pertuzumab is NCCN-listed but not FDA-approved here
Dabrafenib + trametinib — tumor-agnostic accelerated approval. ROAR biliary cohort ORR 47–53%, PFS 9.0 mo
Pembrolizumab (tumor-agnostic, now regular approval) — KEYNOTE-158 cholangiocarcinoma cohort ORR 41%, median OS 24.3 months. Dostarlimab is an alternative
Larotrectinib / entrectinib / repotrectinib for NTRK; selpercatinib for RET (tumor-agnostic, converted to traditional approval in 2026). Pralsetinib has no tumor-agnostic approval
No approved option in biliary cancer. Adagrasib showed activity in a small pan-tumor cohort (5/12); trial or off-label only

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — regimen dosing, the evidence behind adjuvant and local therapy, and trials

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing
rows: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + cisplatin 25 mg/m² on days 1 and 8, with durvalumab 1500 mg day 1 — q21d. Chemotherapy for up to 8 cycles, durvalumab continues
Same gem/cis backbone with pembrolizumab 200 mg day 1, q21d
Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² day 1 + 5-FU 1200 mg/m²/day ×48 h continuous infusion from day 1 — q14d
Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² then gemcitabine 1000 mg/m², days 1, 8, 15 of a 28-day cycle. Single-arm phase 2 that missed its primary endpoint — an alternative, not a standard
1250 mg/m² PO twice daily, days 1–14 of a 21-day cycle, ×8 cycles (6 months). Grade 3 hand-foot in ~20%
Gemcitabine + capecitabine ×4 cycles, then capecitabine with radiation ×6 weeks (45 Gy nodal, 54–59.4 Gy tumor bed)
500 mg PO daily — IDH1-mutant, after 1–2 prior lines
70 mg PO daily — FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement, previously treated, FGFR-inhibitor-naive

blocks.heading: Reading the adjuvant evidence honestly
items: BILCAP is the standard of care but was a formally negative trial. ITT median OS 51.1 vs 36.4 months, HR 0.81, p=0.097 — the primary endpoint was not met. It became practice on the per-protocol analysis (HR 0.75) and a prespecified sensitivity analysis (HR 0.71). Worth knowing when someone asks why capecitabine
SWOG S0809 is single-arm — 2-year OS 65% in resected extrahepatic CCA or gallbladder cancer with pT2-4, node-positive or margin-positive disease. Benchmark data, not a randomized comparison

Negative adjuvant trials: PRODIGE-12 (GEMOX) and BCAT (gemcitabine) both failed. ASCOT showed adjuvant S-1 improves 3-year OS (77.1% vs 67.6%) in an all-Japanese population — but S-1 is not available in the US
ACTICCA-1 (gem/cis vs capecitabine) has closed accrual and has not yet read out — it is the trial that may finally settle this

blocks.heading: Liver-directed therapy — what is actually supported
items: Nothing randomized. Every option below rests on single-arm phase 2 or retrospective data
HAI floxuridine via implanted pump (partial response 58%, median OS 25 months in a single-institution phase 2) — requires an experienced hepatobiliary program
Y-90 / TARE concurrent with first-line chemotherapy: ORR 39%, median OS 22 months, 22% downstaged to surgery — but grade 3–4 toxicity was 71%, and the one randomized trial, SIRCCA, was terminated

Ablative radiation gives excellent local control, but ABC-07 randomized SBRT after chemotherapy and missed its PFS endpoint (8.6 vs 9.0 months). The frequently quoted dose-escalation survival figures come from a retrospective series with heavy selection bias

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Gemcitabine + cisplatin vs gemcitabine — OS 11.7 vs 8.1 mo, HR 0.64. The backbone, since 2010
Add durvalumab to gem/cis — OS 12.8 vs 11.5 mo, HR 0.80; 24-mo OS 24.9% vs 10.4%
Add pembrolizumab to gem/cis — OS 12.7 vs 10.9 mo, HR 0.83. Effectively interchangeable with TOPAZ-1
FOLFOX after gem/cis — OS 6.2 vs 5.3 mo. Median gain is under a month; the honest number is 12-mo OS 25.9% vs 11.4%
Adding nab-paclitaxel to gem/cis — negative. OS 14.0 vs 13.6 mo. Responses rose, survival did not
Adjuvant capecitabine — ITT p=0.097, primary endpoint not met; standard of care on secondary analyses
Adjuvant S-1, Japan — 3-yr OS 77.1% vs 67.6%. Not applicable in the US
Pemigatinib (ORR 37%) and futibatinib (ORR 42%) in FGFR2-altered disease
Lirafugratinib — ORR 46%, DOR 11.8 mo, far less hyperphosphatemia. Approved 23 Sep 2026
Ivosidenib in IDH1-mutant — PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 mo, HR 0.37
Zanidatamab in HER2 IHC 3+ — ORR 52%, DOR 14.9 mo
Dabrafenib + trametinib in BRAF V600E — ORR 47–53%
